speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; have you noticed any abdominal distension or blood in your stool? Please also tell me if you are passing meconium stool normally.

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus. 

Given the bilious vomiting, feeding intolerance, and family history of pyloric stenosis (which shares a similar anatomical vulnerability), the clinical picture is highly suggestive of this life-threatening condition. Immediate surgical evaluation and imaging are required.

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Xray (Upright).
REQUEST TEST: Upper GI Series.
